items.headline: CBS / ToI: Khamenei in Hiding, Reachable Only Via Courier Network — Deal Latency is Structural, Not Signal of Collapse; May 26 Endorsement Stands; FM Formal Text Pending
items.summary: The primary overnight addition to the Iran deal picture is a CBS News report (corroborated by Times of Israel and others, circulating May 25-26) that Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is hiding in an undisclosed location and communicates exclusively via an elaborate network of couriers designed to prevent Israeli assassination. Operational details: (1) even senior Iranian officials have no direct means of contacting him; (2) 'every piece of information he receives is dated and there's a lot of latency to his responses'; (3) the broader Iranian leadership chain is also operating via bunkers and couriers, with one US official characterizing internal Iranian communications as 'almost like watching a sitcom — they are completely exasperated.' The analytical implication for the deal: the May 26 US intelligence characterization that 'Khamenei endorsed the broad template' describes a signal that passed through this courier architecture — dated, with inherent latency. The endorsement remains on record as of this filing and stands as this morning's baseline. The CBS revelation explains WHY the gap between 'Khamenei endorsed template' (May 26 US intel) and 'Iranian FM formal text confirming nuclear commitments' (not yet issued) is structural, not indicative of deal collapse. It also explains the 'Trump real-time optimism vs. Iranian FM qualification' dynamic: Trump's negotiators communicate in real time; Khamenei's authorization arrives dated. The deal is alive. But the courier architecture adds a structural layer of imprecision to intelligence confidence: when US officials say 'Khamenei endorsed,' that assessment reflects a couriered signal of uncertain currency, not a verified direct communication. Iranian FM formal text confirming the nuclear commitment framework remains the key confirmation artifact. WPA: Congress is in session Day 2 post-Memorial Day. No emergency session, no pre-deadline House floor vote, no Senate 10th resolution has been scheduled. The administration's 'hostilities terminated' posture does not survive May 29 plain-text: the naval blockade (Day 46), ongoing CENTCOM self-defense operations, and physical Hormuz closure are operative. A deal signed before May 29 is the cleanest legal exit; no deal has been signed as of this morning.
